title: introduce-delegated-kms-mirroring-and-residency-sampler
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add delegated KMS mirroring sidecar, RBAC v2 bindings for read-only key proofing, and deterministic audit sampling for high-volume tenants. Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag.
description:
Context and motivation:
Customers running in high-throughput, region-pinned workloads reported elevated latency and KMS rate limits when every request required a remote KMS residency proof check. This PR introduces a delegated KMS mirroring component and a deterministic residency audit sampler to reduce blast radius and operational load while preserving compliance signals.

What this PR does (single-line summary):
- Adds a delegated KMS-mirroring sidecar service (kms-mirror) that caches signed residency proofs with TTL and supports read-only mirroring of CMK provenance for eligible tenants.
- Introduces RBAC v2 templates that grant the mirror a scoped, auditable read-only role and an opt-in operator binding for tenants requiring explicit consent.
- Adds a deterministic audit-sampling middleware that marks sampled events with a resumable sampling token and sticky policy per tenant/geozone.
- Wire up observability: exposes metrics (residency_cache_hit, mirror_fetch_latency, sampled_audit_rate) and tracing for end-to-end proof paths.

Design notes and compliance rationale:
- The mirror stores only signed, opaque proofs from customer CMKs and never holds plaintext keys. Proofs are bound to request-nonce + tenant claim and include region assertions to prevent cross-zone reuse. TTL defaults to 12 hours and is configurable per-tenant.
- RBAC v2 bindings are created as a new "mirror-read" role with a narrow policy: allowed actions: kms:prove, kms:fetch-proof. Role can be granted at the tenant or namespace level and includes an immutable audit tag requirement.
- Deterministic sampling uses a stable hash of tenant_id + request_day modulo sample_period to ensure reproducible samples for investigations; default sampling rates differ by compliance tier (e.g., 100% for SOC-high, 10% for standard). Sampled records include a resumable token so auditors can request chained samples.

Checklist (performed):
- [x] Implementation for kms-mirror service (HTTP/GRPC endpoints + internal lease manager).
- [x] RBAC v2 policy templates + migration script to add mirror-read skeleton roles.
- [x] Audit middleware and config knobs exposed in console and operator CRD.
- [x] Unit and integration tests for proof caching and sampling determinism.
- [x] Telemetry dashboards (in draft) and Prometheus metrics.
- [x] End-to-end e2e with private-installer smoke tests behind feature flag.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature guarded under feature flag enable_kms_mirror. Default: off for existing tenants. New tenants with compliance tier SOC-HIGH will get a prompted opt-in during onboarding.
- Rollout: canary 5% of traffic routed to mirror; monitor residency_cache_hit > 60% and error budget. If mirror unavailable, requests fall back to direct KMS proofing path (fail-open pattern triggers extended audit tagging).

Security review highlights:
- Mirror only accepts signed proofs; it validates provenance chain and rejects proofs missing region claim.
- Access to mirror reads requires RBAC mirror-read role; operator token binding is time-bound and audited.
- Added a hardened scrubber that strips PII from any mirrored metadata before storage; audit trails retain only deterministic tokens and cryptographic hashes.

Testing and CI notes:
- Local unit tests cover caching TTL and eviction, RBAC policy parsing, and sampling determinism.
- Integration tests spin up the mirror and a test KMS emulator.
- CI flaky test: auth_integration::session_expiry was intermittently failing in first run; reran and check passed. Full CI green on merge.

Operational runbooks (short):
- If mirror_fetch_latency > 300ms sustained, switch canary to fallback-only and open incident handler.
- If cache hit ratio drops below 40% for > 15m, investigate proof churn and TTL misconfiguration.

Related work:
- complements ENG-2810 (kvs-prefix-ttl) and ENG-3699 (rbac-v2-policy-compiler) and references SUP-1143 customer escalation.

Notes for reviewers:
- The RBAC policy templates are intentionally conservative; please focus reviews on policy scoping and audit tag flow.
- Pay attention to the sampling token format (stable hex string) — auditors will rely on chaining.

Merge rationale:
This reduces KMS call volume for high-throughput tenants, improves tail latency for region-pinned requests, and provides compliant, auditable proof caching that can be toggled per tenant. The change is behind flag and includes fallback and rescind procedures.

review_conversation: Diego Rivera: Can the mirror be used to replay proofs across regions? We need to ensure region binding is cryptographically enforced.
Maya Patel: It cannot. Proofs include region assertion signed by the CMK provider and the mirror validates the assertion before storing. Added test case to assert mismatched region rejection.
Hannah Cho: Sampling token exposes a hash derived from tenant id. Is there any risk of reconstructability?
Maya Patel: Token is HMAC(tenant_id || date || secret) with rotating key; secret stays in KMS and mirror never stores it. Added security note to docs and unit tests for token uniqueness.
Samir Khan: RBAC role looks broad at namespace-level grants; prefer tenant-scoped by default. Please add migration to grant at tenant level and allow operator override.
Maya Patel: Updated migration to create tenant-scoped roles and added an operator override flag. Updated PR to include migration script path.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge. Changelog entry added and feature flag default left off. Post-merge: scheduled canary for 2026-03-10 with 5% traffic and monitoring dashboard link added to release notes.
